definition: What it represents is a comparison between two steady values: the previous steady-state value, T_o, and the new slider setting, T_s. Their difference, T_s − T_o, is the gap the whole rest of the chain has to close — its size says how far the temperature has to travel, and its sign says which way: up if T_s > T_o, down if T_s < T_o. Nothing has heated or cooled yet at this step; the difference operator only measures the change that has been asked for.
name: Difference operator

definition: What it represents is two signals combined into one by adding them: the pair of the difference operator, for the places where a signal is genuinely the sum of two parts. Its place in this note is the system diagram in section 11, where T_H(x) — the position part of the pad signal, a constant — adds with T_H(t) — the time part, an oscillator. Because T_H(x) is constant, the output of the adding is an oscillator that just becomes T_H(t) again: adding a constant to the oscillator does not change its kind. Adding is this operator; multiplying is the mixer, ⊗; subtracting is the difference operator.
name: Addition operator — the adder, ⊕

definition: What it represents is a signal that swings around a target value and settles onto it: it overshoots, comes back, overshoots less, and the swings die away inside a decaying envelope until only the target remains. That is the true shape of the temperature signals in this note before they are simplified: T_H(t) at the pad is an oscillator signal, and after the medium change T_air(t) is another — the air swings around the pad temperature as it closes in on it. The smooth exponential is this signal with the swing removed (simplification 6), not the signal itself.
name: Oscillator signal

definition: What it represents is the spread of energies across all the particles of the air at one instant — few nearly still, most in the middle, a long tail of a few racing — and the temperature that spread amounts to. It stands for two steps: simplification 3, the whole set of particles and their bounces replaced by this one distribution, and simplification 4, that distribution collapsed by its integral average, ⟨E⟩ = ∫ E · P(E) dE = (3/2) k_B T, into the single number T. It is made before the diagram even starts and carried through the whole chain — every temperature anywhere in the diagrams is already this average, not any one particle's motion.
name: Boltzmann distribution

definition: What it represents is the signal crossing from one medium into another — here, heat passing from the solid heating pad into the air — and coming out as the corresponding signal in the new medium: T_H(t) becomes T_air(t). The two sides are not the same substance and do not respond the same way: the pad is held at its temperature by the thermostat, while the air has to be brought there by contact. The medium-change math: the air chases the pad by Newton's law, dT_air/dt = k·(T_H − T_air), so T_air(t) = T_H − (T_H − T_o)·e^(−kt) as its mean — an oscillator in the air, swinging around the pad temperature, with the coupling k set by the contact between pad and air. The kind of signal does not change across it: oscillator in, oscillator out — what changes is the medium carrying it, and with it the constants that govern it.
name: Medium change

definition: What it represents is the envelope of an oscillator signal being taken as the signal. An oscillator swings around its mean inside a decaying envelope; this converter — a type of signal converter — keeps that envelope and the mean it bounds, and drops the swing between them, so an exponential comes out where an oscillator went in. It changes the kind of signal, not its destination or its size: the exponential it produces settles to the same target, along the same mean, as the oscillator it replaces. This is simplification 6 as a step in the diagram — a conversion we perform on the signal so the rest of the chain can work with the simple form, not a process happening in the tank.
name: Envelope signal converter — the envelope operator

definition:
What it represents is a signal that closes on its target at a rate proportional to the gap that remains — fast while the gap is big, slowing as the gap shrinks, levelling off as it arrives: the Newton settling of section 5, T(t) = T_s − (T_s − T_o)·e^(−kt). It is the simplified form of the oscillator signal — the oscillator's envelope and mean with the swing removed — and it is the form the envelope signal converter puts out. It appears twice in the chain: once as that converter's output, and once again after the mixer, because attenuation scales an exponential's size without changing its kind — the signal at position x is still this same exponential settling, only weaker. Whether it climbs or falls is set by the signal itself, by the sign of T_s − T_o: heating and cooling are the same exponential, closing the gap from opposite sides.

The equivalent diagrams. This symbol can be drawn four ways — the curve climbing or falling, toward the right or toward the left — and all four are equivalent symbols: each one stands for the same exponential signal, the same closing-on-the-target at a rate proportional to the gap. When the direction is specifically known, the drawing that matches it can be used: heating, T_s > T_o, climbs — drawn here up to the right, the form this note uses — and cooling, T_s < T_o, falls. But when the direction is unknown, the four are interchangeable: any one of them can be drawn, and it still means the exponential — the direction is then carried by the signal itself, by the sign of T_s − T_o, not by which way the curve in the circle happens to lean.
name: Exponential signal

definition: What it represents is one signal scaling another by multiplication: a transform carried out as a product. In this note the mixer is where the temperature signal meets space: the exponential T_air(t) runs through the attenuation and is multiplied by it — T_air(t) × α(x) = T_air(t) at position x — so what comes out is the same signal, reduced by exactly the factor the distance x imposes. The mixer does not add anything of its own; it applies one input to the other. (Addition is a different operation — the adder, ⊕, defined beside the difference operator above.)
name: Mixer — ⊗

definition: What it represents is a transform converter for attenuation. A transform converter is a block in a system diagram that takes a transform in one form and puts it out in another form: it changes the form of the transform — the form of the response — not the kind of signal — the underlying transform, what it does to the signal, stays exactly the same; only the form it is carried in changes. That is what separates it from the envelope signal converter (the envelope operator): an envelope signal converter changes the kind of signal (oscillator in, exponential signal out), while a transform converter changes the form a response is expressed in. A transform converter has no letter notation — it is named for the conversion it performs. This converter works on the attenuation over distance: in goes the attenuation as it actually is in space — an exponential decay, the signal weakening smoothly and steadily with distance from the panel — and out comes the same attenuation converted into a piecewise linear approximation: straight-line pieces standing in for the smooth exponential. The attenuation itself is unchanged — the same weakening, at the same distances — only the form it is carried in changes. This symbol is not used in the Temperature block diagram — the attenuation there is carried as the exponential itself, in the exponential curve below the mixer — but it is kept here because it can be used later.
name: Piecewise linear approximation

definition: What it represents is keeping only the settled part of a signal and discarding its transient: a filter in time, not in space. It stands for the judgement that the variable has been held constant long enough — t ≥ t_s, where t_s is the time the settling takes — that the travel from the old value to the new one can be ignored and only the arrived value kept. It is a filter because it passes part of what reaches it and holds back the rest: the steady state passes, the transient does not. This is simplification 8 as a step in the diagram, and it applies only when that condition actually holds — move the slider and the transient is real again until it settles.
name: Steady-state filter

definition: What it represents is a signal that no longer changes: one value, held. It is the end of the chain — the temperature at position x after the transient has been filtered away, T constant at steady state — the state the whole system was travelling toward from the moment the difference operator measured the gap. Every earlier step exists to produce this: a settled temperature, at a place, that stays where it is until the setting changes again.
name: Constant signal
